chart.Keywords: trend, time-series, line, growth, timeline, progress, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: Data has a time axis; user needs to observe rise/fall trends or rate of change over a continuous period
chart.When NOT to Use: Fewer than 4 data points (use stat card); more than 6 series (visual noise); no time dimension exists
chart.Data Volume Threshold: <1000 pts: SVG; ≥1000 pts: Canvas + downsampling; >10000: aggregate to intervals
chart.Color Guidance: Primary: #0080FF. Multiple series: distinct colors + distinct line styles. Fill: 20% opacity
chart.Accessibility Notes: Use solid, dashed, and dotted line styles plus direct series labels; never distinguish series by hue alone.
chart.A11y Fallback: Visible data table plus concise trend summary. Keyboard: focus reveals hover values; +/- buttons zoom; Reset restores the full range.

chart.Keywords: compare, categories, bar, comparison, ranking, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: Comparing discrete categories by magnitude; ranking or ordering is the core insight; categories ≤ 15
chart.When NOT to Use: Categories > 15 (use table or search); data has time dimension (use line); showing proportions (use waffle/stacked)
chart.Data Volume Threshold: <20 categories: vertical bar; 20–50: horizontal bar; >50: paginated table
chart.Color Guidance: Each bar: distinct color. Grouped: same hue family. Always sort descending by value
chart.Accessibility Notes: Use direct category/value labels and group outlines or patterns; never encode category solely by bar color. Do not rely on color alone.
chart.A11y Fallback: Visible sortable data table plus concise comparison summary. Keyboard: focus reveals hover values; focusable headers with Enter/Space sort and aria-sort reports direction.

chart.Keywords: part-to-whole, pie, donut, percentage, proportion, share, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: ≤5 categories; one dominant segment vs rest; emphasis on visual proportion over exact values
chart.When NOT to Use: Categories > 5; slice differences < 5% (visually indistinguishable); user needs precise values; accessibility-first context
chart.Data Volume Threshold: Max 6 slices; beyond that switch to stacked bar 100%
chart.Color Guidance: 5–6 max colors. Contrasting palette. Largest slice at 12 o'clock. Always label slices with %
chart.Accessibility Notes: Pie charts do not inherently fail WCAG; unlabeled color-only slices are inaccessible. Use direct labels and patterns, with a non-pie fallback. Do not rely on color alone.
chart.A11y Fallback: Percentage data table and concise part-to-whole summary; offer a stacked bar view. Keyboard: focus reveals slice values; Enter/Space drills in; Back button returns.

chart.Keywords: correlation, distribution, scatter, relationship, pattern, cluster, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: Exploring relationship between two continuous variables; identifying clusters or outliers in a dataset
chart.When NOT to Use: Variables are categorical (use grouped bar); fewer than 20 points (patterns aren't meaningful); mobile-primary context
chart.Data Volume Threshold: <500 pts: SVG; 500–5000: Canvas at 0.6–0.8 opacity; >5000: hexbin or aggregate first
chart.Color Guidance: Color axis: gradient (blue → red). Bubble size: relative to 3rd variable. Opacity: 0.6–0.8 to show density
chart.Accessibility Notes: Combine marker shapes with direct group labels; color may reinforce but must not be the only distinction.
chart.A11y Fallback: Visible data table plus correlation summary. Keyboard: focus reveals point values; labeled start/end range inputs replace brush dragging.

chart.Keywords: heatmap, heat-map, intensity, density, matrix, calendar, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: Showing intensity/density across a 2D grid; time-based patterns (e.g., activity by hour × day)
chart.When NOT to Use: Fewer than 20 cells (use bar); user needs to read exact values; colorblind users without pattern fallback
chart.Data Volume Threshold: Up to 10,000 cells efficiently; beyond that aggregate; calendar heatmap: 365 cells max per SVG
chart.Color Guidance: Gradient: Cool (blue) to Hot (red). Divergent scale for ±data. Always include numeric color legend
chart.Accessibility Notes: Print values or symbols in cells and use texture/labels in addition to the color scale. Do not rely on color alone.
chart.A11y Fallback: Grid data table plus intensity summary. Keyboard: focus reveals cell values; +/- buttons zoom; Reset restores the grid.

chart.Keywords: geographic, map, location, region, geo, spatial, choropleth, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: Data has a regional/location dimension; spatial distribution is the core insight for the user
chart.When NOT to Use: Regions have very different sizes making visual comparison misleading (use bar); mobile-primary context
chart.Data Volume Threshold: <1000 regions: SVG; ≥1000: Canvas/WebGL (Deck.gl); global maps: tile-based rendering
chart.Color Guidance: Single color gradient per region group. Categorized colors for discrete types. Legend with clear scale breaks
chart.Accessibility Notes: Label regions directly and pair fills with boundaries or patterns; location meaning cannot depend on color alone.
chart.A11y Fallback: Sortable region table plus geographic summary. Keyboard: arrow keys or labeled pan buttons move the map; +/- buttons zoom; Enter drills into a focused region; Back returns.

chart.Keywords: funnel, flow, conversion, drop-off, pipeline, stages, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: Sequential multi-stage process; showing conversion or drop-off rates between defined stages
chart.When NOT to Use: Stages aren't sequential; values don't decrease monotonically (use bar); fewer than 3 stages
chart.Data Volume Threshold: 3–8 stages optimal; beyond 8 stages group minor steps into 'Other'
chart.Color Guidance: Stages: single color gradient (start → end). Show conversion % between each stage. Highlight biggest drop
chart.Accessibility Notes: Keep stage names and values visible and distinguish stages with text and boundaries, not only a gradient. Do not rely on color alone.
chart.A11y Fallback: Linear stage table/list plus conversion summary. Keyboard: focus reveals stage values; Enter/Space drills in; Back returns.

chart.Keywords: performance, target, kpi, gauge, goal, threshold, progress, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: Single KPI measured against a defined target or threshold; dashboard summary context
chart.When NOT to Use: No target or benchmark exists; comparing multiple KPIs at once (use bullet chart grid)
chart.Data Volume Threshold: Single metric per gauge; for 3+ KPIs use bullet chart grid layout
chart.Color Guidance: Performance: Red → Yellow → Green gradient. Target: marker line. Threshold zones clearly differentiated
chart.Accessibility Notes: Place the number and target text beside the gauge and label threshold zones; red/yellow/green alone is insufficient.
chart.A11y Fallback: Visible KPI/target text and a one-row data table plus status summary. Keyboard: focus reveals the same detail as hover.

chart.Keywords: forecast, prediction, confidence, band, projection, estimate, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: Historical data + model predictions; communicating uncertainty range to non-technical stakeholders
chart.When NOT to Use: No historical baseline; prediction confidence is too low to be useful; audience is not data-literate
chart.Data Volume Threshold: Keep historical window to 30–90 days for readability; forecast horizon ≤ 30% of visible x-axis range
chart.Color Guidance: Actual: solid line #0080FF. Forecast: dashed #FF9500. Confidence band: 15% opacity fill same hue
chart.Accessibility Notes: Use solid actual and dashed forecast lines, direct labels, and a named confidence range; hue alone is insufficient.
chart.A11y Fallback: Visible forecast table plus uncertainty summary. Keyboard: focus reveals hover values; buttons toggle actual/forecast; +/- buttons zoom; Reset restores range.

chart.Keywords: anomaly, outlier, spike, alert, detection, monitoring, deviation, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: Monitoring a time-series for outliers; alerting users to unexpected spikes or dips in operational data
chart.When NOT to Use: Anomalies are predefined categories (use bar with highlight); real-time context without a pause control
chart.Data Volume Threshold: Stream at ≤60fps with Canvas; batch: up to 10,000 pts; mark anomalies as a separate data layer
chart.Color Guidance: Normal: #0080FF solid line. Anomaly marker: #FF0000 circle + filled. Alert band: #FFF3CD background zone
chart.Accessibility Notes: Mark anomalies with a distinct shape and text annotation as well as color. Do not rely on color alone.
chart.A11y Fallback: Anomaly event list/table plus narrative alert summary. Keyboard: focus reveals point details; alerts are available in the persistent list without hover.

chart.Keywords: hierarchy, nested, treemap, parent, children, breakdown, drill, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: Showing size relationships within a hierarchy; overview of proportional structure (e.g., budget breakdown)
chart.When NOT to Use: Hierarchy depth > 3 levels (too complex to read); user needs to compare sibling values precisely
chart.Data Volume Threshold: <200 nodes: SVG; 200–1000: Canvas; >1000: paginate or pre-filter before rendering
chart.Color Guidance: Parent nodes: distinct hues. Children: lighter shades of same hue. White separator borders: 2–3px
chart.Accessibility Notes: Label hierarchy nodes and use borders/patterns as well as hue; make the tree table the primary accessible view. Do not rely on color alone.
chart.A11y Fallback: Collapsible tree table plus hierarchy summary; treemap remains supplementary. Keyboard: focus reveals hover values; Enter/Space drills or expands; Back collapses/returns.

chart.Keywords: flow, process, sankey, distribution, source, target, transfer, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: Showing how quantities flow between nodes; multi-source multi-target distribution
chart.When NOT to Use: Flow directions form loops (use network graph); fewer than 3 source-target pairs; mobile-primary context
chart.Data Volume Threshold: <50 flows: SVG; ≥50: Canvas; >200 flows: aggregate minor flows into 'Other' node
chart.Color Guidance: Gradient from source to target color. Flow opacity: 0.4–0.6. Node labels always visible
chart.Accessibility Notes: Label source, target, and value; use line style or node symbols in addition to gradient color. Do not rely on color alone.
chart.A11y Fallback: Source-to-target flow table plus flow summary. Keyboard: focus reveals hover values; Enter/Space drills into a node; Back returns.

chart.Keywords: waterfall, cumulative, variance, incremental, bridge, delta, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: Showing how individual positive/negative components add up to a final total (e.g., P&L, budget variance)
chart.When NOT to Use: Changes are not additive; more than 12 bars (readability breaks); audience expects a simple total
chart.Data Volume Threshold: 4–12 bars optimal; beyond 12 aggregate minor items into a single 'Other' bar
chart.Color Guidance: Increases: #4CAF50. Decreases: #F44336. Start total: #2196F3. End total: #0D47A1. Running total line: dashed
chart.Accessibility Notes: Pair increase/decrease bars with signed values and directional icons, not red/green alone. Do not rely on color alone.
chart.A11y Fallback: Running-total table plus variance summary. Keyboard: focus reveals the same value as hover.

chart.Keywords: radar, spider, multi-variable, attributes, dimensions, comparison, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: Comparing multiple entities across the same fixed set of attributes (e.g., product feature comparison)
chart.When NOT to Use: Axes > 8 (unreadable); values need precise comparison (use grouped bar); audience unfamiliar with radar charts
chart.Data Volume Threshold: 2–3 datasets maximum per chart; 5–8 axes; beyond 8 axes switch to parallel coordinates
chart.Color Guidance: Single dataset: #0080FF at 20% fill. Multiple: distinct hues with 30% fill. Border: full opacity
chart.Accessibility Notes: Use line styles, point shapes, and direct series labels in addition to color. Do not rely on color alone.
chart.A11y Fallback: Raw data table and grouped-bar alternative plus comparison summary. Keyboard: focus reveals values; buttons toggle series.

chart.Keywords: stock, trading, ohlc, candlestick, finance, price, volume, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: Financial time-series with Open/High/Low/Close data; trading or investment product context only
chart.When NOT to Use: Non-financial audience; no OHLC data available (use line chart); accessibility-first context
chart.Data Volume Threshold: Real-time: Canvas required. Historical: paginate by time range. Max 500 candles visible at once
chart.Color Guidance: Bullish: #26A69A. Bearish: #EF5350. Volume bars: 40% opacity below. Body fill vs hollow for OHLC style
chart.Accessibility Notes: Use filled versus hollow candles and OHLC text values; bullish/bearish meaning cannot depend on color. Do not rely on color alone.
chart.A11y Fallback: Sortable OHLC table plus daily-change summary. Keyboard: focus reveals candle values; +/- buttons zoom; Reset restores range; live updates do not steal focus.

chart.Keywords: network, graph, nodes, edges, connections, relationships, force, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: Mapping connections between entities; network topology or social graph exploration context
chart.When NOT to Use: Node count > 500 without clustering pre-applied; user needs precise connection counts; mobile context
chart.Data Volume Threshold: ≤100 nodes: SVG; 101–500: Canvas; >500: must apply clustering/LOD before rendering
chart.Color Guidance: Node types: categorical colors. Edges: #90A4AE at 60% opacity. Highlight path: #F59E0B
chart.Accessibility Notes: Use labeled node types, shapes, and edge styles in addition to color; the adjacency view is the accessible source of truth. Do not rely on color alone.
chart.A11y Fallback: Adjacency list/table and relationship summary; tree view when applicable. Keyboard: focus reveals node details; Enter drills; Move up/down/left/right buttons replace drag.

chart.Keywords: distribution, statistical, spread, median, outlier, quartile, boxplot, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: Showing spread, median, and outliers of a dataset; comparing distributions across multiple groups
chart.When NOT to Use: Fewer than 20 data points per group (distribution is not meaningful); audience unfamiliar with statistical charts
chart.Data Volume Threshold: Any sample size; aggregated representation so rendering is ⚡ Excellent at any volume
chart.Color Guidance: Box fill: #BBDEFB. Border: #1976D2. Median line: #D32F2F bold. Outlier dots: #F44336
chart.Accessibility Notes: Label median, quartiles, whiskers, and outliers directly; do not use color alone for statistical roles.
chart.A11y Fallback: Statistics table plus distribution summary. Keyboard: focus reveals the same statistics as hover.

chart.Keywords: bullet, compact, kpi, dashboard, target, benchmark, range, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: Dashboard with multiple KPIs side by side; space-constrained contexts where a gauge is too large
chart.When NOT to Use: Single KPI with emphasis (use gauge); data has no defined target range; fewer than 3 KPIs
chart.Data Volume Threshold: Ideal for 3–10 bullet charts in a grid; scales to any count efficiently
chart.Color Guidance: Qualitative ranges: #FFCDD2 / #FFF9C4 / #C8E6C9 (bad/ok/good). Performance bar: #1976D2. Target: black 3px marker
chart.Accessibility Notes: Label every qualitative range and target with text; color is supplementary.
chart.A11y Fallback: Visible KPI/target table plus status summary. Keyboard: focus reveals the same detail as hover.

chart.Keywords: waffle, percentage, proportion, progress, filled, grid, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: Showing what fraction of a whole is filled; percentage progress in a visually engaging and accessible format
chart.When NOT to Use: More than 5 categories (use stacked bar); exact values matter over visual proportion; very tight space
chart.Data Volume Threshold: 10×10 grid standard (100 cells); for > 5 categories switch to stacked 100% bar
chart.Color Guidance: 3–5 categories max. 2–3px gap between cells. Each category a distinct accessible color pair
chart.Accessibility Notes: Label each category and percentage and add patterns or symbols; filled-cell color alone is insufficient.
chart.A11y Fallback: Percentage table/list plus part-to-whole summary. Keyboard: focus reveals each cell value.

chart.Keywords: sunburst, hierarchy, nested, proportion, radial, circle, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: Exploring nested proportions where both hierarchy and relative size matter (e.g., org spend breakdown)
chart.When NOT to Use: More than 3 hierarchy levels (outer rings become unreadable); precision matters over overview; mobile
chart.Data Volume Threshold: <100 nodes: SVG; 100–500: Canvas; >500: filter to top N before rendering
chart.Color Guidance: Center to outer: darker to lighter hue. Each level 15–20% lighter. Contrasting border between sectors
chart.Accessibility Notes: Label hierarchy levels and segments and use boundaries/patterns as well as hue; the indented list is primary. Do not rely on color alone.
chart.A11y Fallback: Collapsible indented list/table plus hierarchy summary and breadcrumbs. Keyboard: Enter/Space drills or expands; Back button returns; focus reveals hover detail.

chart.Keywords: root cause, decomposition, tree, hierarchy, drill-down, ai-split, attribution, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: Decomposing a metric into contributing factors; AI-assisted analysis or BI drill-down scenarios
chart.When NOT to Use: No clear parent-child causal relationship; audience expects a summary rather than exploration
chart.Data Volume Threshold: Up to 5 levels deep; limit visible nodes to 20 per level for readability; lazy-load deeper levels
chart.Color Guidance: Positive impact nodes: #2563EB. Negative impact nodes: #EF4444. Neutral connectors: #94A3B8
chart.Accessibility Notes: Name each node and contribution and use shapes/connector styles in addition to color. Do not rely on color alone.
chart.A11y Fallback: Expandable tree table plus root-cause summary. Keyboard: Enter/Space drills and expands; Back collapses; dedicated expand/collapse buttons expose the same operations.

chart.Keywords: 3d, spatial, immersive, terrain, molecular, volumetric, point-cloud, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: Scientific/engineering context where Z-axis carries essential info not expressible in 2D
chart.When NOT to Use: 2D projection conveys the same insight; mobile context; accessibility-required environments; standard business dashboards
chart.Data Volume Threshold: WebGL required. Deck.gl: up to 1M points. Three.js: LOD required beyond 50,000 pts
chart.Color Guidance: Depth cues: lighting and shading. Z-axis: color gradient (cool → warm). Transparent overlapping: opacity 0.4
chart.Accessibility Notes: Use labels, shapes, and depth-independent cues; color and 3D position cannot be the only carriers of meaning.
chart.A11y Fallback: Mandatory 2D projection, data table, and spatial summary. Keyboard: rotate/pan buttons and +/- zoom controls replace pointer/VR manipulation; Reset returns the camera.

chart.Keywords: streaming, real-time, ticker, live, velocity, pulse, monitoring, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: Live monitoring dashboards; IoT/ops data updating at ≥1 Hz; user needs current value at a glance
chart.When NOT to Use: Update frequency < 1/min (use periodic-refresh line chart); flashing content without reduced-motion support
chart.Data Volume Threshold: Canvas/WebGL required. Buffer last 60–300s of data. Downsample older data on scroll
chart.Color Guidance: Current pulse: #00FF00 (dark theme) or #0080FF (light theme). History: fading opacity. Grid: dark background
chart.Accessibility Notes: Show the current value and status text and use line styles or markers in addition to color. Do not rely on color alone.
chart.A11y Fallback: Streaming data table plus current-value/trend summary. Keyboard: Pause/Resume button controls updates; focus reveals values; +/- buttons zoom; Reset restores range.

chart.Keywords: sentiment, emotion, nlp, opinion, feeling, text-analysis, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: NLP output visualization; exploratory analysis of text corpus sentiment; frequency-weighted keyword overview
chart.When NOT to Use: Precise values matter (word size is inherently imprecise); screen-reader context; corpus < 50 items
chart.Data Volume Threshold: 50–5000 terms optimal. Beyond 5000: apply top-N filtering before render. Avoid on mobile
chart.Color Guidance: Positive: #22C55E. Negative: #EF4444. Neutral: #94A3B8. Word size maps to frequency
chart.Accessibility Notes: Expose every term, count, and sentiment as text; size and color are supplementary only.
chart.A11y Fallback: Sortable term table/list plus sentiment summary; word cloud is supplementary. Keyboard: focus reveals word details; labeled controls filter with Space/Enter.

chart.Keywords: process, mining, variants, path, bottleneck, log, event, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
chart.When to Use: Analyzing event logs to visualize actual process flows; identifying bottlenecks and deviations in ops/product funnels
chart.When NOT to Use: No event log data available; audience expects a static flowchart (use diagram tool); node count > 100 without pre-filtering
chart.Data Volume Threshold: <30 nodes: SVG; 30–100: Canvas; >100: apply variant filtering (top 80% of cases) before rendering
chart.Color Guidance: Happy path: #10B981 thick line. Deviations: #F59E0B thin line. Bottleneck nodes: #EF4444 fill
chart.Accessibility Notes: Label nodes and paths and use shapes/line styles in addition to color; bottlenecks require text annotations. Do not rely on color alone.
chart.A11y Fallback: Path summary table plus bottleneck narrative. Keyboard: Move buttons replace drag; focus reveals node details; Enter activates a node; Back returns.

ux.Description: Some CSS properties trigger expensive repaints
ux.Do: Use transform and opacity for animations

ux.Description: Easing should match how an element changes speed and purpose

ux.Description: Stacking context conflicts cause hidden elements

ux.Description: Hidden overflow can clip important content

ux.Description: Fixed elements can overlap or be inaccessible

ux.Description: Adjacent touch targets need adequate spacing
ux.Do: Minimum 8px gap between touch targets

ux.Description: Custom gestures can conflict with system
ux.Do: Avoid horizontal swipe on main content

ux.Description: 300ms tap delay feels laggy
ux.Do: Use touch-action CSS or fastclick

ux.Description: Accidental refresh is frustrating
ux.Do: Disable where not needed

ux.Description: Tactile feedback improves interaction feel
ux.Do: Use for confirmations and important actions

ux.Description: Keyboard focus, including controls inside a modal, needs a visible indicator

ux.Description: Visual feedback on interactive elements
ux.Do: Change cursor and add subtle visual change

ux.Description: Show immediate feedback on press/click

ux.Description: Clearly indicate non-interactive elements

ux.Description: Prevent double submission during async actions
ux.Do: Disable button and show loading state

ux.Description: Users need to know when something fails
ux.Do: Show clear error messages near problem

ux.Description: Confirm successful actions to users
ux.Do: Show success message or visual change

ux.Description: Prevent accidental destructive actions
ux.Do: Confirm before delete/irreversible actions

ux.Description: Text must be readable against background
ux.Do: Minimum 4.5:1 ratio for normal text

ux.Description: Don't convey information by color alone
ux.Do: Use icons/text in addition to color

ux.Description: Images need text alternatives

ux.Description: Screen readers use headings for navigation
ux.Do: Use sequential heading levels h1-h6
ux.Don't: Skip heading levels or misuse for styling

ux.Description: Interactive elements need accessible names
ux.Do: Add aria-label for icon-only buttons

ux.Description: Web users need complete keyboard navigation with visible focus on every operable control
ux.Do: Keep tab order aligned with visual order and test every action without a pointer
ux.Don't: Keyboard traps or illogical tab order

ux.Description: Content should make sense when read aloud
ux.Do: Use semantic HTML and ARIA properly

ux.Description: Inputs must have associated labels
ux.Do: Use label with for attribute or wrap input

ux.Description: Error messages must be announced
ux.Do: Use aria-live or role=alert for errors

ux.Description: Allow keyboard users to skip navigation

ux.Don't: No skip link on nav-heavy pages

ux.Description: Large images slow page load
ux.Do: Use appropriate size and format (WebP)

ux.Description: Load content as needed
ux.Do: Lazy load below-fold images and content

ux.Description: Large bundles slow initial load
ux.Do: Split code by route/feature

ux.Description: Repeat visits should be fast
ux.Do: Set appropriate cache headers

ux.Description: Web fonts can block rendering
ux.Do: Use font-display swap or optional

ux.Description: External scripts can block rendering
ux.Do: Load non-critical scripts async/defer

ux.Description: Large JavaScript slows interaction
ux.Do: Monitor and minimize bundle size

ux.Description: CSS/JS can block first paint
ux.Do: Inline critical CSS defer non-critical

ux.Description: Every input needs a visible label
ux.Do: Always show label above or beside input

ux.Description: Each invalid field needs an inline error connected to that field
ux.Do: Show a specific error below the input and reference it with aria-describedby
ux.Don't: Show only a top-level error without identifying each invalid field

ux.Description: Validate as user types or on blur
ux.Do: Validate on blur for most fields

ux.Description: Use appropriate input types
ux.Do: Use email tel number url etc

ux.Description: Help browsers autofill correctly
ux.Do: Use autocomplete attribute properly

ux.Description: Mark required fields clearly
ux.Do: Use asterisk or (required) text

ux.Description: Let users see password while typing
ux.Do: Toggle to show/hide password

ux.Description: Confirm form submission status
ux.Do: Show loading then success/error state

ux.Description: Inputs should look interactive
ux.Do: Use distinct input styling
ux.Don't: Inputs that look like plain text

ux.Description: Show appropriate keyboard for input type
ux.Do: Use inputmode attribute

ux.Description: Design for mobile then enhance for larger
ux.Do: Start with mobile styles then add breakpoints

ux.Description: Test at all common screen sizes

ux.Description: Text must be readable on all devices

ux.Description: Set viewport for mobile devices

ux.Description: Avoid horizontal scrolling
ux.Do: Ensure content fits viewport width

ux.Description: Images should scale with container
ux.Do: Use max-width: 100% on images

ux.Description: Tables can overflow on mobile

ux.Description: Adequate line height improves readability

ux.Description: Long lines are hard to read

ux.Description: Consistent type hierarchy aids scanning
ux.Do: Use consistent modular scale

ux.Description: Fonts should load without layout shift
ux.Do: Reserve space with fallback font

ux.Description: Body text needs good contrast
ux.Do: Use darker text on light backgrounds

ux.Description: Headings should stand out from body
ux.Do: Clear size/weight difference

ux.Description: Loading feedback should match the expected wait and avoid flashing for near-instant work

ux.Description: Guide users when no content exists
ux.Do: Show helpful message and action

ux.Description: Help users recover from errors
ux.Do: Provide clear next steps

ux.Description: Show progress for multi-step processes
ux.Do: Step indicators or progress bar

ux.Description: Transient messages for non-critical info
ux.Do: Auto-dismiss after 3-5 seconds

ux.Description: Confirm successful actions

ux.Description: Elements should respond to eye tracking before pinch

ux.Description: WCAG 2.2 AA requires keyboard focus to remain at least partially visible
ux.Do: Offset sticky UI with scroll-padding and dismiss or move persistent overlays
ux.Don't: Let headers footers banners or chat widgets fully cover focus

ux.Description: WCAG 2.2 AAA requires keyboard focus to remain fully visible
ux.Do: Keep the entire focused component unobscured by author-created content
ux.Don't: Present this enhanced AAA criterion as an AA requirement or allow persistent UI to hide any part of focus
ux.Code Example Good: close persistent overlay before focus moves behind it
ux.Code Example Bad: sticky footer covers half the focused button

ux.Description: WCAG 2.2 AAA defines minimum area and contrast for focus indicators
ux.Do: Use an indicator at least as large as a 2 CSS px perimeter with 3:1 state contrast
ux.Don't: Present this enhanced AAA criterion as an AA requirement or use a thin low-contrast outline

ux.Description: WCAG 2.2 AA requires a single-pointer alternative for author-controlled drag operations
ux.Do: Add buttons menus or tap-to-move controls and retain keyboard operation
ux.Don't: Make dragging the only way to reorder resize or select
ux.Code Example Good: Move up and Move down buttons beside drag handle

ux.Description: WCAG 2.2 AA requires 24 CSS px pointer targets or an applicable exception
ux.Do: Use at least 24 by 24 CSS px or verify spacing equivalent inline user-agent or essential exceptions
ux.Don't: Assume native 44pt or 48dp guidance defines web conformance

ux.Description: WCAG 2.2 A requires repeated help mechanisms to stay in the same relative order
ux.Do: Keep contact self-help and automated help in consistent locations
ux.Don't: Move help controls to different locations on each page

ux.Description: WCAG 2.2 A avoids requiring the same information twice in one process
ux.Do: Auto-populate prior values or let users select previously entered information
ux.Don't: Ask users to retype the same address or account data without necessity

ux.Description: WCAG 2.2 AA says authentication must not depend only on a cognitive function test unless an exception applies
ux.Do: Allow password managers and paste; offer passkeys OAuth or another non-cognitive method
ux.Don't: Block paste or require manual OTP transcription with no alternative

ux.Description: Auto-rotating content needs user control
ux.Do: Provide previous next and play/pause; stop on focus or hover and when reduced motion is requested
ux.Don't: Auto-advance slides without a stop control

ux.Description: An error summary for failed validation complements inline field errors and must be easy to find by keyboard and screen reader users
ux.Do: Place it at the top of the form; move focus to its heading or container after failed submit; link each item to its invalid field; retain inline errors
ux.Don't: Replace inline errors with a visual-only summary or move focus on every blur
ux.Code Example Good:
There is a problem

Enter an email address
ux.Code Example Bad: Toast only with no field links or focus target

ux.Description: Short multi-line headings may use balanced wrapping as a progressive visual heuristic
ux.Do: Bound the measure and test natural-wrap fallback across widths fonts and locales
ux.Don't: Promise an exact final line or insert blanket nonbreaking spaces or hardcoded br tags
ux.Code Example Bad: Heading copy rewritten with forced last-line breaks

ux.Description: URLs identifiers and user content must not force horizontal overflow
ux.Do: Use overflow-wrap anywhere and let flex or grid text children shrink
ux.Don't: Apply word-break break-all to all prose

ux.Description: Text must remain available at narrow widths zoom and user spacing overrides
ux.Do: Use fluid sizes content-driven height and unitless line height
ux.Don't: Clip text in fixed-width or fixed-height boxes

ux.Description: Headings actions errors safety text and distinguishing names need complete access
ux.Do: Wrap stack resize or provide a visible full-detail path
ux.Don't: Clamp essential meaning only to make cards uniform
ux.Code Example Good: Action label wraps or opens full details
ux.Code Example Bad: Primary action shown only as an unexplained ellipsis

ux.Description: Badges communicate state while chips or tags represent values or actions
ux.Do: Choose static or interactive markup from the label's meaning and ownership
ux.Don't: Make every pill clickable or encode status with color alone

ux.Description: Filter chips and editable value collections must preserve labels when space or text size changes
ux.Do: Wrap the collection or use an operable +n disclosure for hidden overflow values
ux.Don't: Force all chips into one clipped row or hide overflow values

ux.Description: A badge chip or pill label should stay whole on one line when practical and disclose unavoidable truncation
ux.Do: Bound only unpredictable values; use nowrap with a shrinkable label; expose full text to keyboard pointer and touch users
ux.Don't: Let one compact label wrap to a second line or use a hover-only tooltip
ux.Code Example Good: Flexible label with min-width 0 and an operable full-value disclosure
ux.Code Example Bad: Fixed-width badge wraps to second line or clips with title-only recovery

ux.Description: Interactive chips need a native role accessible name state keyboard operation and visible focus
ux.Do: Prefer a button and expose pressed or selected state that matches the visible label
ux.Don't: Use a clickable div or reveal the only action on hover

ux.Description: Async badge and count changes should announce a meaningful contextual status without moving focus
ux.Do: Use one appropriate atomic status message such as 3 items in cart
ux.Don't: Announce a bare number or make every badge a competing live region

ux.Description: Rapid compact-control changes can interrupt an in-flight transition
ux.Do: Cancel or replace prior motion; set the final semantic state directly and handle cancellation cleanup
ux.Don't: Depend on animationend or transitionend for required state correctness
ux.Code Example Bad: Enable the chip only inside transitionend

react.Description: Move await into branches where actually used to avoid blocking unused code paths
react.Do: Move await operations into branches where they're needed
react.Don't: Await at top of function blocking all branches
react.Code Example Good: if (skip) return { skipped: true }; const data = await fetch()
react.Code Example Bad: const data = await fetch(); if (skip) return { skipped: true }

react.Description: Execute independent async operations concurrently using Promise.all()
react.Code Example Bad: const user = await fetchUser(); const posts = await fetchPosts()

react.Description: Use better-all for operations with partial dependencies to maximize parallelism
react.Do: Use better-all to start each task at earliest possible moment
react.Don't: Wait for unrelated data before starting dependent fetch
react.Code Example Good: await all({ user() {}, config() {}, profile() { return fetch((await this.$.user).id) } })
react.Code Example Bad: const [user, config] = await Promise.all([...]); const profile = await fetchProfile(user.id)

react.Description: In API routes start independent operations immediately even if not awaited yet
react.Do: Start promises early and await late
react.Code Example Good: const sessionP = auth(); const configP = fetchConfig(); const session = await sessionP
react.Code Example Bad: const session = await auth(); const config = await fetchConfig()

react.Description: Use Suspense to show wrapper UI faster while data loads
react.Do: Wrap async components in Suspense boundaries
react.Don't: Await data blocking entire page render
react.Code Example Bad: const data = await fetchData(); return <DataDisplay data={data} />

react.Description: Import directly from source files instead of barrel files to avoid loading unused modules
Use next/dynamic to lazy-load large components not needed on initial render
react.Don't: Import heavy components at top level
react.Code Example Good: const Monaco = dynamic(() => import('./monaco'), { ssr: false })

react.Description: Load analytics and logging after hydration since they don't block interaction
react.Code Example Good: const Analytics = dynamic(() => import('@vercel/analytics'), { ssr: false })

react.Description: Load large data or modules only when a feature is activated
Preload heavy bundles on hover/focus before they're needed
Use React.cache() for server-side request deduplication within single request
react.Don't: Fetch same data multiple times in tree
react.Code Example Good: export const getUser = cache(async () => await db.user.find())
react.Code Example Bad: export async function getUser() { return await db.user.find() }

react.Description: Use LRU cache for data shared across sequential requests
react.Don't: Refetch same data on every request
react.Code Example Good: const cache = new LRUCache({ max: 1000, ttl: 5*60*1000 })

react.Description: Only pass fields that client actually uses across RSC boundaries
react.Do: Pass only needed fields to client components

react.Description: Restructure components to parallelize data fetching in RSC
react.Do: Use component composition for parallel fetches

react.Description: Use Next.js after() to schedule work after response is sent
Use SWR for automatic request deduplication and caching
react.Do: Use useSWR for client data fetching

react.Description: Share global event listeners across component instances
Don't subscribe to state only used in callbacks
react.Don't: Subscribe to state used only in handlers
react.Code Example Good: const handleClick = () => { const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search) }
react.Code Example Bad: const params = useSearchParams(); const handleClick = () => { params.get('ref') }

react.Description: Extract expensive work into memoized components for early returns
react.Don't: Compute expensive values before early return
react.Code Example Good: const UserAvatar = memo(({ user }) => ...); if (loading) return <Skeleton />
react.Code Example Bad: const avatar = useMemo(() => compute(user)); if (loading) return <Skeleton />

react.Description: Specify primitive dependencies instead of objects in effects
react.Do: Use primitive values in dependency arrays

react.Description: Subscribe to derived booleans instead of continuous values
react.Code Example Bad: const width = useWindowWidth(); const isMobile = width < 768

react.Description: Use functional setState updates for stable callbacks and no stale closures
Pass function to useState for expensive initial values
react.Do: Use function form for expensive init

react.Description: Mark frequent non-urgent state updates as transitions
react.Don't: Block UI on every state change

react.Description: Wrap SVG in div and animate wrapper for hardware acceleration
Apply content-visibility: auto to defer off-screen rendering
Extract static JSX outside components to avoid re-creation
react.Do: Hoist static elements to module scope
react.Code Example Good: const skeleton = <div class='animate-pulse' />; function C() { return skeleton }

react.Description: Use inline script to set client-only data before hydration
react.Do: Inject sync script for client-only values

react.Description: Use ternary instead of && when condition can be 0 or NaN
Use Activity component to preserve state/DOM for toggled components
react.Do: Use Activity for expensive toggle components

react.Description: Group CSS changes via classes or cssText to minimize reflows
react.Don't: Change styles one property at a time

react.Description: Build Map for repeated lookups instead of multiple .find() calls
react.Do: Build index Map for O(1) lookups
react.Code Example Good: const byId = new Map(users.map(u => [u.id, u])); byId.get(id)
react.Code Example Bad: users.find(u => u.id === order.userId) // O(n) each time

react.Description: Cache object property lookups in hot paths
Use module-level Map to cache repeated function results
react.Do: Use Map cache for repeated calls
react.Code Example Good: const cache = new Map(); if (cache.has(x)) return cache.get(x)

react.Description: Cache localStorage/sessionStorage reads in memory
Combine multiple filter/map into single loop

react.Description: Check array lengths before expensive comparisons
react.Code Example Good: if (a.length !== b.length) return true; // then compare
react.Code Example Bad: a.sort().join() !== b.sort().join() // even when lengths differ

react.Description: Return early when result is determined to skip processing
react.Don't: Process all items then check errors

react.Code Example Bad: function C() { const re = new RegExp(pattern); re.test(x) }

react.Description: Use loop for min/max instead of sort - O(n) vs O(n log n)

react.Description: Use Set/Map for O(1) lookups instead of array.includes()
react.Do: Convert to Set for membership checks

react.Description: Use toSorted() instead of sort() to avoid mutating arrays

react.Keywords: useeffectevent effect event non-reactive latest values
react.Description: Read non-reactive latest values inside Effects without re-synchronizing the Effect
react.Do: Use useEffectEvent only for non-reactive logic called from inside Effects; keep real reactive dependencies
react.Don't: Use Effect Events to hide dependencies or call them from render or ordinary event handlers
react.Code Example Good: const onConnected = useEffectEvent(() => notify(theme)); useEffect(() => { connection.on('connected', onConnected) }, [roomId])
react.Code Example Bad: useEffect(() => connect(roomId, theme), [roomId]) // hides reactive theme use

react.Description: Use refs only when a latest value must be read without causing a render
react.Do: Synchronize the ref after commit and read current from asynchronous callbacks
react.Don't: Mutate ref.current during render or use refs to bypass reactive dependencies
